# Community code of conduct

Rostrum exists to make event work calmer, more legible, and more accountable.
We expect the project space to feel the same way.

## Our standards

Participants should:

- be respectful, specific, and generous in technical disagreement;
- welcome people across experience levels, identities, backgrounds, and access
  needs;
- critique ideas and changes, not people;
- protect private event, speaker, reviewer, and security information;
- make room for questions and acknowledge mistakes without humiliation;
- consider the people who operate, review, speak at, and attend events—not only
  the code path.

Harassment, threats, discriminatory language, unwanted sexual attention,
doxxing, deliberate exposure of private data, and sustained personal attacks
are not acceptable.

## Scope and enforcement

This standard applies in repository discussions, reviews, issues, and project
spaces where someone represents Rostrum. Report conduct concerns privately to
the repository owner through the channel supplied with your collaboration or
evaluation access. Do not expose a target or reporter in a public issue.

Maintainers may edit or remove content, pause a discussion, restrict
participation, or remove access when needed to protect the community. Reports
will be considered in context and shared only with people needed to resolve
them. This project does not currently publish a response-time SLA.
